'''Jasper Donald Rine''' (born 1953) is an American scientist, a member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]],<ref name=":0">[http://nrc88.nas.edu/pnas_search/memberDetails.aspx?ctID=20017381 Jasper Rine at] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111106114639/http://nrc88.nas.edu/pnas%5Fsearch/memberDetails.aspx?ctID=20017381 |date=2011-11-06 }} [[PNAS]] website</ref> and a Professor of Genetics, Genomics and Development at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].

Rine received his [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] from the [[State University of New York at Albany]] in 1975 and his [[Ph.D.]] in [[molecular genetics]] from the [[University of Oregon]] in 1979. He then joined the Berkeley [[Faculty (teaching staff)|faculty]] in 1982. He is also a former director of the Human Genome Center at [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]] and a fellow of the [[American Academy of Microbiology]], an honorific leadership group of the [[American Society for Microbiology]]. As a graduate student with [[Ira Herskowitz]] Rine codiscovered yeast [[SIR protein]]s, conserved chromatin organizing proteins that modulate gene expression across taxa. As a professor, Rine was also one of the organizers of the [[Dog Genome Project]]. He was named a [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] professor in 2006.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hhmi.org/scientists/jasper-rine|title=Jasper Rine|website=HHMI.org}}</ref> His work focuses on [[epigenetics]] and understanding the impact of human genetic variation.

==Stolen laptop incident==
In 2005, a video was posted online depicting Rine speaking before a class and explaining that his laptop, which he stated contained extremely sensitive data from various sources, had been stolen. He attempted to scare the thief—whom Rine believed to be one of the students—into confessing by claiming the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]] was looking into the matter,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sg.news.yahoo.com/2005-04-21-dont-steal-laptops-from-berkeley-professors-ever.html|title=Don't steal laptops from Berkeley professors. Ever.|first=Barb|last=Dybwad|date=April 21, 2005|publisher=Engadget|website=sg.news.yahoo.com}}</ref> along with making up an elaborate bluff on how the device was being tracked. Many people with tech knowledge saw through this and called him out for it online.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://finance.yahoo.com/news/2005-04-25-laptop-thief-not-scared-by-berkeley-profs-made-up-threats.html|title=Laptop thief not scared by Berkeley prof's made-up threats|first=Barb|last=Dybwad|date=April 25, 2005|publisher=Engadget|website=finance.yahoo.com}}</ref>
